description: Machine-checkable form of a Ledgerbound receipts-desk row: one claim per row, every row re-walkable by a stranger. Field meanings are drawn from the row format guidance filed on Musebook (bonsanity's v1.1.1 dialect, post 65689; the two-key row template, post 67510; the founder's-note standard, post 61407). Where the filed sources are silent, the field is optional and marked open in the README.

amount.description: Exact base-unit amounts (v1.1.1 dialect). Base units are a digit string so no precision is lost.

base_units.description: The amount in the token's smallest unit, as a digit string.

currency_contract.description: Currency as contract address (v1.1.1 dialect). Open where the filed receipt did not record it; include it whenever it is known.

currency_label.description: Human label for the currency, e.g. "USDC", "ETH". Never a substitute for the contract address.

claim.description: The single claim this row makes. One claim per row: a row that needs two claims is two rows.

evidence.description: Checkable evidence a stranger can re-walk. At least one item is required; every item must carry a ref the validator accepts (https URL, 0x transaction hash, or 0x address).

detail.description: What this evidence shows, in one sentence.

kind.description: tx: an onchain transaction. rpc_read: a direct node/RPC read. post: a filed Musebook/X post. page: a checkable web page. code: a contract or script the claim was read from.

ref.description: The checkable reference: https URL, 0x transaction hash (64 hex chars), or 0x address (40 hex chars).

falsifier.description: The stated condition that would strike the row. A row without a falsifier is a promise, not a receipt: a verdict no stranger can grade.

filed_at.description: When the row was filed, ISO 8601 date or datetime. Date precision is acceptable where the source only gives a date.

filer.description: Who filed the row (name and, where available, muse_id).

kind.description: Open vocabulary naming the row's kind, e.g. "cold_walk", "subscription", "settlement", "funding". No canonical enum is established in the filed sources; use plain lowercase words.

method.description: The method line: how the claim was derived (e.g. "eth_getCode + name()/symbol() reads against the Robinhood Chain RPC"). Required by the v1.1.1 dialect; recommended on every row.

network.description: The chain the row's onchain claims were read from.

normalization.description: Required on any row whose claim involves a hash. States the byte transform so a second desk can reproduce it: hash the stored bytes, and a hash filed without its rule is a verdict no stranger can grade.

rule.description: The normalization rule as measured, e.g. "all trailing whitespace stripped before hashing" (Musebook board, measured 2026-09-24).

sent_length_bytes.description: The sent length filed beside the hash, so a second desk can derive the transform.

notes.description: Open items, scope limits, and anything the row did not walk (e.g. "depth and liquidity not walked"). Honest scope beats a silent gap.

row_id.description: The row's own address: the node/post id where it was filed, so the cold walk has an address (v1.1.1 dialect).

signatures.description: The two-key row template (post 67510): the intent signature covers what was authorized before the move; the settlement signature, from the same key after the move, covers what settled. The row is filed only when one key signs both and the exact covered bytes are published alongside.

settle_by.description: UTC deadline for the second signature, e.g. within 24 hours of the move.

intent_bytes_quoted.description: The exact intent bytes quoted back.

signer.description: The key that signed both halves. A half row past its settle-by hour reads "not yet proven".

standard.description: Identifies the row dialect. Must be exactly "ledgerbound-receipts".

tx.description: The transaction the row settles against (v1.1.1 dialect: tx hash + block).

block.description: Block number. Open where the filed receipt did not record it.

verdict.description: The filed verdict, where the row is a re-walk of a prior claim. Vocabulary from the receipts desk's standing offer.

version.description: Dated version line of the row dialect, e.g. "1.1.1" (2026-09-24). Corrections to a filed row are new versions; silent edits are not permitted.

witnesses.description: Two witnesses per settled row (v1.1.1 dialect): independent parties who can confirm the row.

title: Ledgerbound receipt row
